messages.subject: Calling nimble from a package
parts:
Hi nimbleRs,

I seem to be experiencing a problem similar to https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/issues/894 -- but the issue was closed last November. I have a package which creates input for nimble (code, data, initial values), runs the MCMC, and summarizes the output. Everything works if I load the code package with devtools::load_all(). However, it doesn't work when build,install, and load the package with library(). The error messages indicate that certain functions (expit, nimSwitch) can't be found. I've copied the full output below.

I'm running nimble version 0.9.1 on an up-to-date Windows 10 machine with R 4.0.0, but I see the same behaviour on an HPC running CentOS with R version 3.5.2 and 4.0.0. 

Has anybody else seem similar problems with the latest version. Is there a workaround?

Cheers,

Simon

Hi all,

I want to share the solution back out to the listserv in case it's useful for others.

Essentially, when NIMBLE is needed by a package, it must be placed in the Depends field of the package's DESCRIPTION file, not the Imports field. This has to do with how the package's namespace is created in the R environment; only when assigned to Depends is the nimble package namespace constructed properly. nimble's dynamic code generation has necessitated a lot of under-the-hood namespacing solutions and tricks, and right now it appears these tricks don't work properly unless the namespace is constructed independently of other packages, as it is when added to Depends.

We may address this issue in future releases, but for now, please put nimble in Depends when using nimble to support other packages.

Thanks,
Ben

messages.subject: Re: Calling nimble from a package
parts:
Hi all,

I found another solution and thought I'd post it here so it's documented. nimble can be included as a suggested package in another package (i.e., under Suggests in the description) by using the commands:

requireNamespace(nimble)
attachNamespace("nimble")

The first line is the recommended mechanisms for loading suggested packages. The second which I've added attaches the namespace so that functions in the package can be seen globally. This avoids direct use of library(nimble) within the package which generates a note when the package is checked.

I have a feeling that this may be counter to the spirit of not using library() (I think I've essentially recreated what library() does), but it works and does not raise any issues during the checks.

Thanks all for your help,

Simon

Hi Simon, thanks for this.

I believe that if a package is in Suggests, then one is supposed to access functions using the namespace resolution operator. So instead of using `attachNamespace`, one would have code that looks like this:

requireNamespace(nimble)
## some code ##
nimble::nimbleModel(...)
## more code ##
nimble::configureMCMC(...)

-chris
